action: Duplicate existing training observations with replacement; no new independent information.
limitation: Does not need neighbors but can memorize rare wines. Use the same conservative target caps as SMOTE.
k=1,2,3 is feasible with four inner-training quality-3 wines; feasibility is not robust independent evidence. Keep targets conservative.

action: Generate from minority points classified as in danger using a local one-versus-rest neighborhood; borderline-1 interpolates within class.
limitation: Do not infer boundaries from four quality-3 or six-eight quality-8 inner-training wines. Keep these classes unchanged. Use m=5, audit safe/danger/noise anchors, and compare with matched SMOTE on 4/7. No-danger classes receive no additions; never silently substitute ordinary SMOTE.

action: Allocate more generated samples to minority observations with more other-class neighbors.
limitation: With tiny genuine classes this local difficulty estimate can amplify noise/overlap. Installed implementation rounds per-point allocations, can miss exact caps or generate zero rows at small budgets. A capped allocation redesign would be a separate method; no claim of universal unsuitability.

action: Follow SMOTE with edited-nearest-neighbor removal of observations whose local labels disagree.
limitation: Default cleaning targets every class and may discard legitimate minority boundary wines. With tiny genuine counts this is too aggressive for the initial comparison. A protected ENN design needs separate removal controls; computational feasibility would not establish statistical suitability.

action: Follow capped SMOTE with removal of specified-class endpoints of mutual nearest-neighbor pairs having different labels.
limitation: Clean only qualities 5/6; never remove genuine or generated minority rows. This differs explicitly from default all-class cleaning. Audit all removed real rows and retained support; cleaning may still discard useful majority boundary information.
